references.text: The previous verse where the Lord commands Moses to make a bronze serpent and set it on a pole, so that those who were bitten could look at it and live.
King Hezekiah broke the bronze snake that Moses had made, because the Israelites had been burning incense to it and calling it Nehushtan.
Jesus compares himself to the snake that was lifted up in the wilderness, saying that the Son of Man must be lifted up in the same way, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.
Jesus speaks about the Son of Man being lifted up, which points back to the bronze snake that was lifted up for salvation.
Jesus says that when he is lifted up from the earth, he will draw all people to himself, a parallel to the bronze snake that was lifted up to give life.
